1.plain: Trains the hidden weight matrices inside the transformer blocks with Muon (Nesterov momentum, then Newton–Schulz orthogonalization) and the embedding, output head, norm gains and biases with AdamW.
bullets: Muon learning rate 0.02 for the hidden matrices
Muon weight decay 0.01
Flat learning rate, then linear decay to zero over the last 70%
Attention and MLP output projections and the head start at zero

2.plain: Replaces Muon with ordinary AdamW on the hidden matrices and adds a 250-step warmup, giving an Adam reference point that the benchmark notes is likely undertuned.
bullets: Hidden matrices switch from Muon to AdamW
AdamW learning rate 0.0015 on hidden matrices
Hidden weight decay 0.01 → 0.1
250-step linear warmup for every parameter group

3.plain: Retunes the baseline by raising both the Muon learning rate and weight decay by 25%, leaving the optimizer code, schedule shape and init unchanged.
bullets: Muon learning rate 0.02 → 0.025
Muon weight decay 0.01 → 0.0125

4.plain: Replaces Muon with AdamH, an Adam step taken on a hyperball that keeps each hidden matrix's norm fixed at its initial value, so weight decay is dropped.
bullets: Per-element Adam direction instead of orthogonalized momentum
Nonzero, scaled-up init for output projections and MLP inputs
Hidden learning rate decays over the whole run, AdamW over last 40%
250-step warmup for the hidden learning rate

5.plain: Applies Muon's update as a hyperball step that holds hidden-matrix norms at their initial values, so the learning rate sets a relative step and weight decay is dropped.
bullets: Step length set to learning rate times weight norm, then renormalized
Nonzero, scaled-up init for output projections and MLP inputs
Hidden learning rate decays from the start, AdamW over last 40%
Muon learning rate 0.02 → 0.018

6.plain: Doubles the Muon weight decay to 0.025 and switches to Gaussian init for hidden weights with all biases at zero; the two changes were not tested separately.
bullets: Muon weight decay 0.0125 → 0.025
Hidden weights Gaussian instead of uniform, similar scale
All biases start at zero

7.plain: Switches to Muon², which divides the momentum elementwise by a running RMS of the gradient before orthogonalizing, balancing per-coordinate scales first, and raises the learning rate fourfold.
bullets: Adam-style second-moment scaling before Newton–Schulz
Muon learning rate 0.025 → 0.10
Second-moment decay 0.95, no bias correction

8.plain: Adds NorMuon to MuonH: each row of the orthogonalized update is divided by its running RMS, evening out update size across neurons before the hyperball step.
bullets: Per-row running RMS normalization after Newton–Schulz
Wide MLP output matrices normalized per column instead
Result claimed 25 steps before the learning rate reaches zero
Normalizer decay 0.95, no bias correction

9.plain: Adds NorMuon-lite row normalization and an update-to-weight floor that enlarges small updates, replacing weight decay as the way to keep relative step sizes from shrinking as weights grow.
bullets: Update norm floored at 0.35 times the weight norm
Weight decay no longer applied to hidden matrices
NorMuon-lite: per-row RMS normalization, overall norm kept
Muon learning rate 0.02 → 0.0375

10.plain: Switches the hidden matrices to NorMuon, which evens out update size across neurons while keeping Muon's overall step size, and raises the learning rate to 0.035.
bullets: Per-row running RMS normalization after Newton–Schulz
Update rescaled back to its original overall norm
Muon learning rate 0.025 → 0.035
Result claimed 50 steps before the learning rate reaches zero

11.plain: Adds Contra-Muon, which subtracts a small multiple of the spectrally normalized momentum from the orthogonalized update, giving dominant momentum directions slightly smaller steps than weak ones.
bullets: Subtracts 0.2 times the normalized momentum after Newton–Schulz
Momentum normalized by its top singular value
Result rescaled back to the orthogonalized update's norm

12.plain: Raises the Muon learning rate from 0.025 to 0.035, borrowing NorMuon's tuned value, and claims its result 25 steps before the learning rate reaches zero.
bullets: Muon learning rate 0.025 → 0.035
Result claimed 25 steps before the learning rate reaches zero
Denser validation near the end to fix the stop step

13.plain: Wraps NorMuonH and AdamW in a MuLoCo outer loop: every 30 steps the net weight change drives an outer Nesterov step that extrapolates past the inner optimizer's endpoint.
bullets: Outer Nesterov SGD step every 30 inner steps
Outer learning rate 0.7, applied to all parameters
Overshoots the inner endpoint by up to about 40%
Hidden-matrix norms can drift at each outer step

14.plain: Adds SOAP preconditioning to the MLP matrices, whitening the momentum Adam-style in the gradient's eigenbasis before Newton–Schulz orthogonalizes it.
bullets: SOAP whitening before Newton–Schulz, MLP matrices only
Eigenbasis refreshed every 10 steps
Contra-Muon now uses the preconditioned momentum
Result claimed 25 steps before the learning rate reaches zero

15.plain: Adds Newton-Muon, which whitens each hidden gradient by the inverse of its layer's input covariance before the Muon step, and gives each matrix type its own learning rate.
bullets: Gradient multiplied by inverse input covariance before momentum
Covariance re-estimated and inverted every 64 steps
Learning rate and weight decay split by matrix type
Possibly inactive: compilation may skip the statistics collection (unverified)

16.plain: Extends SOAP preconditioning to the attention output projections, with a trust gate that falls back toward raw momentum when the SOAP direction disagrees, down-weighting stale whitening.
bullets: SOAP extended to attention output projections; query, key, value unchanged
Trust gate mixes SOAP and raw momentum by agreement
Gate kept within fixed bounds early in training
SOAP denominator floored at 0.2 of its RMS

17.plain: Replaces plain Newton–Schulz orthogonalization on the MLP matrices with Aurora, which rebalances rows first so no single neuron gets an outsized share of the update.
bullets: Aurora row balancing before Newton–Schulz on MLP matrices
Square attention matrices keep plain Newton–Schulz
NorMuon-lite normalization dropped, unmentioned by the authors
Gaussian hidden init and zero biases

18.plain: Adds PMuon's two-sided preconditioner before Newton–Schulz, damping momentum directions that have been consistently large on either side, while keeping the parent's learning rate and weight decay.
bullets: Running left and right covariances of the momentum
Inverse 0.3 power of each covariance applied
Eigenbases tracked with one QR step per iteration

19.plain: Replaces NorMuon's orthogonalized direction with KL-SOAP, which runs Adam in an eigenbasis built from KL-Shampoo statistics, while keeping the hyperball step and the parent's init and schedules.
bullets: No Newton–Schulz: Adam step in a rotated eigenbasis
Eigenbasis from KL-Shampoo factors, refreshed every step
Adam momentum 0.95 in the eigenbasis
First step only initializes the preconditioner

20.plain: Adds the PowerCool power-law cooldown and a time-varying update: Contra-Muon fades out by step 2000, then the update blends toward Soft-Muon, which gives stronger directions larger steps.
bullets: PowerCool cooldown; training stops before the rate reaches zero
Late blend toward Soft-Muon, capped at 80%
Attention SOAP moved from output projections to value matrices
Update-to-weight floor 0.35 → 0.3825

21.plain: Replaces Muon with Shampoo, preconditioning the momentum by inverse fourth roots of left and right gradient covariances, with each step's size borrowed from Adam (grafting).
bullets: Inverse fourth-root preconditioners, recomputed every 5 steps
Step size grafted from Adam, matrix by matrix
Learning rate 0.035 → 0.0015
Decoupled weight decay 0.025 → 0.2

22.plain: Turns off Muon's momentum so each step orthogonalizes the raw minibatch gradient, isolating how much Muon gains from momentum; it needs roughly 2.5 times as many steps.
bullets: Muon momentum 0.95 → 0, pure spectral descent
Learning rate 0.035 → 0.03
Weight decay 0.025 → 0.015
Result claimed 275 steps before the schedule ends

23.plain: Replaces Muon with Muown, splitting each weight row into an Adam-trained length and a direction moved by orthogonalized steps whose angular size shrinks on a schedule; no weight decay.
bullets: Row lengths trained by Adam, row directions by orthogonalized momentum
Scheduled growth of the direction's norm shrinks angular steps
Power-law cooldown that ends after training stops
AdamW learning rates raised two- to threefold

24.plain: Splits the learning-rate cooldown so the hidden matrices decay over the last 80% of training while AdamW parameters hold their peak rate until the last 40%.
bullets: Muon decay window: last 70% → last 80%
AdamW decay window: last 70% → last 40%

25.plain: Replaces both linear decays with a power-law cooldown above small learning-rate floors and stops training before the schedule ends, so final learning rates stay above zero.
bullets: Power-law decay with exponent 1.5 replaces linear
KL-SOAP learning-rate floor at 1.7% of peak
AdamW learning-rate floor at 4% of peak
Training stops 85 steps before the schedule ends

26.plain: Replaces NorMuon with SinkSOAP, which skips Newton–Schulz and instead balances the momentum's rows and columns with Sinkhorn iterations inside the gradient's eigenbasis, a SOAP-like generalization of Muon.
bullets: No Newton–Schulz: Sinkhorn balancing in a rotated basis
Gradient Gram eigenbases recomputed every step
NorMuon normalization kept only for the MLP matrices
Learning rate 0.035 → 0.04

27.plain: Swaps KL-SOAP for standard SOAP inside the hyperball step and gives the hidden matrices a power-law learning-rate decay whose horizon extends past the end of training.
bullets: Plain Shampoo statistics replace KL-Shampoo for the eigenbasis
Hidden learning-rate decay exponent 1 → 1.25
Hidden schedule ends 75 steps after training stops
Momentum kept in the original basis, not rotated

28.plain: Switches to DynMuon, which reshapes the orthogonalized update with a scheduled exponent on the singular values, mildly favoring weak directions for most of training.
bullets: Spectral exponent: slightly positive early, about -0.25 later
Cheap polynomial approximation, much weaker than an exact power
Muon weight decay 0.01 → 0.025
Gaussian hidden init and zero biases

29.plain: Adds a radial brake that halves the part of each update pushing weights outward, then pins each matrix's norm after the step so sideways moves no longer inflate it.
bullets: Outward radial part of the update scaled by 0.5
Inward radial part left untouched
Norm reset after each step, removing sideways norm creep
Brake applied before the update-to-weight floor

30.plain: Adds Aurora to the MLP output matrices so each MLP neuron gets a near-equal update share, turns off Soft-Muon and NorMuon-lite, and lengthens the Contra-Muon fade.
bullets: Aurora balancing on the MLP output matrices only
Turns off Soft-Muon and NorMuon-lite
Muon momentum ramps 0.85 → 0.95, then back down late
New inits: depth-scaled MLP inputs, randomly tilted norm gains

31.plain: Adds a fading Contra-Muon term and NorMuon-lite, which roughly equalizes per-row angular steps, to Muown's direction updates, and retunes the learning-rate and norm schedules.
bullets: Contra-Muon on direction updates, fading out by step 1925
NorMuon-lite with short memory, decay 0.8
Muown learning rate 0.00325 → 0.0045
Shorter, retuned learning-rate and norm-growth schedules

32.plain: Adds a SODA-style pull of each hidden matrix toward its initial value, with strength shrinking over time, so early updates are gradually forgotten before the pull fades out late.
bullets: Weights mixed toward initial values before each update
Mixing weight shrinks like one over the step count
Pull cosine-faded to zero by step 2750
Acts as decay toward zero for zero-initialized output projections

33.plain: Replaces Muon with PSGD, whose Kronecker-factored preconditioner is fitted every step to whiten the momentum, and applies the result through a norm-preserving hyperball step without weight decay.
bullets: Kronecker preconditioner refit every step against a random probe
PSGD learning rate 0.025, decaying linearly from the start
Nonzero, per-module scaled init; nothing starts at zero
AdamW decays over second half, only to 10% of peak

34.plain: Adds late reduced-rank extrapolation (RRE) of the hidden weights: a capped jump every 5 steps from step 2820 that in practice pulls weights back, like iterate averaging.
bullets: Extrapolation from the last 4 weight snapshots
Each jump damped and capped at 0.1% of weight norm
Optimizer momentum and SOAP statistics left untouched
Training stops at step 2925; schedules unchanged

35.plain: Retunes Shampoo to recompute undamped pseudo-inverse roots every step with shorter memory, tracking recent gradient geometry closely; though labeled one-sided, it still preconditions both sides.
bullets: Pseudo-inverse roots with no damping term
Roots recomputed every step instead of every 5
Learning rate 0.0015 → 0.01
Statistics decay 0.95 → 0.9 for factors and graft

36.plain: Retunes hyperparameters only: higher AdamW learning rates with light weight decay, and a lower Muon learning rate with stronger weight decay; this became the official baseline.
bullets: Muon learning rate 0.035 → 0.025
Muon weight decay 0.025 → 0.05
AdamW learning rates raised, embedding 0.3 → 0.7
AdamW weight decay 0 → 0.001

37.plain: Grafts the tuned AdamW settings from the #36 baseline onto MuonH, scaled up further and with a longer AdamW cooldown, leaving MuonH itself unchanged.
bullets: AdamW learning rates raised, embedding 0.3 → 0.91
AdamW decay window: last 40% → last 85%
AdamW weight decay 0 → 0.001
Output head no longer zero-initialized

38.plain: Retunes the late phase (Tempered-Polar, tighter radial brake, higher update-to-weight floor) and, for evaluation only, moves weights back along recent updates and toward a step-2375 snapshot.
bullets: Final eval blends weights 7.5% back toward an earlier snapshot
Evals from step 2500 shift hidden weights back along recent updates
Tempered-Polar: slight late tilt back toward raw momentum
Outward radial brake tightened 0.5 → 0.4 late

39.plain: Wraps the Muon and AdamW optimizers in EMA-Nesterov, which shifts weights along a slow average of recent displacements before each gradient computation, acting as an extra long-horizon momentum.
bullets: Lookahead along a 0.99 moving average of weight changes
Shift size 0.6, shrinking with the learning-rate schedule
Shifts applied only from step 500 to 2400

40.plain: Wraps the full optimizer in EMA-Nesterov, an extra momentum that shifts weights along a slow average of recent displacements before each gradient, and shortens the schedules.
bullets: Lookahead along a 0.99 moving average of weight changes
Shift size 0.3, shrinking with the AdamW learning rate
Shifts applied only from step 300 to 1950
Run length 3020 → 2900 steps, schedules shifted earlier

41.plain: Adds Circuit-Muon, which couples each attention head's value and output updates so the head's combined value-output map changes in a balanced way as their norms evolve.
bullets: Each head's value and output updates scaled by partner's inverse size
Pure rescaling direction of each pair projected out
Each matrix's overall update norm left unchanged

42.plain: Zero-initializes all biases, drops the random norm-gain init, and evaluates late weights blended 7.5% back toward a step-2375 snapshot, the same readout as #38.
bullets: Late evals use weights blended 7.5% toward an earlier snapshot
Query, key, value and MLP input biases start at zero
Random norm-gain init dropped; all gains start at 1
Training stops at step 2860, before schedules finish

43.plain: Adds fixed late pulses that move weights back along their recent path (TrailDelta, BroadDelta) and final readouts toward an earlier anchor, while training ends at a higher learning rate.
bullets: TrailDelta: two pull-backs along the last 100 steps' path
BroadDelta: one small pull-back at step 2400
Final readout moves weights 8% toward an earlier anchor
Cooldown end pushed later at step 2600, raising the learning rate

44.plain: Extends SOAP to every hidden matrix with the eigenbasis refreshed each step, removes Circuit-Muon, Contra-Muon and Aurora, and gives biases longer second-moment memory in Adam.
bullets: SOAP on all hidden matrices, eigenbasis refreshed every step
Removes Circuit-Muon, Contra-Muon and Aurora
1-D Adam without bias correction; longer memory for biases
Momentum cooldown doubled to 200 steps

45.plain: Adds a Tail-EMA readout: at step 2720 the weights are blended 60% toward their 150-step moving average to cancel late oscillation noise, and training stops there.
bullets: Moving average of non-embedding weights from step 2000
Average time constant 150 steps
One-time 60% blend toward the average before final eval
Training stops mid-cooldown, schedules unchanged

46.plain: Replaces the matrix-level update-to-weight floor with a per-row floor, adds Cautious Weight Decay on coordinates already shrinking, and makes the Tail-EMA blend an evaluation-only readout.
bullets: Each update row floored at 0.3825 times its weight row's norm
Cautious weight decay 0.025, only on coordinates the step shrinks
Tail-EMA blend used only for evaluation; weights restored
Training runs the full schedule instead of stopping early
